# Welcome {.unnumbered .unlisted}

This is the online version of **Python for R Programmers: A
One-Week Boot Camp for R Users Learning Python** by The
rgtlab Curriculum Project. We have written it for statisticians
and data analysts who are already fluent in R and want to
become productive in Python.

We begin from what a working R user needs in order to read,
write, and run everyday scientific Python: the Python mental
model and how it differs from R; the core data structures and
control flow; NumPy and pandas for numerical and tabular work;
the visualization and modeling stack; and reproducible
project structure with interoperability back to R. The book is
designed for **five consecutive days** of work, roughly one
hour of lecture content each day and two hours of homework,
with no examinations.

The organizing principle is translation. We assume the reader
already knows the R idiom, so we introduce every Python
construct by contrast with its R counterpart. That is, we do
not teach programming from scratch. We teach a second language
to a reader who already thinks in a first one. Each chapter
opens with an R idiom the reader knows, develops the Python
equivalent, and returns to compare what each language makes
easy and what each makes awkward.

This workshop is a companion to a broader curriculum series:

- **R for Biostatistics: A One-Week Boot Camp**
  (<https://r-bootcamp.rgtlab.org>), the preparatory volume
  for the R language this workshop assumes.
- **Git and GitHub for Biostatistics: A One-Week Boot Camp**
  (<https://git-bootcamp.rgtlab.org>), the parallel
  preparatory volume for version control.
- [*Statistical Computing in the Age of AI*](https://scai.rgtlab.org),
  introductory methods (linear models, GLM, mixed
  models, survival, Bayesian, bootstrap, simulation).
- [*Applied Generative AI for Health Sciences Research*](https://applied-genai.rgtlab.org),
  capability classes, RAG, agents, evaluation,
  regulation, deployment.

A reader who has completed *R for Biostatistics* has the R
fluency this workshop assumes. A reader who completes this
workshop should be able to move between the two languages as
a given problem demands.

The reader is referred to the [Preface](preface.qmd) for the
design rationale and to the [Conventions](conventions.qmd)
page for the visual cues used throughout.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
The [Contents](contents.qmd) page lists every chapter on one page.
:::
